body.statement: Determine whether deciding \(r(G,s)\leq3\) for finite simple bow-free ADMGs with singleton target \(s\) has a polynomial-time algorithm, or whether it is \(\mathsf{coNP}\)-complete, using the fixed-point hedge oracle to certify \(r(G,s)>3\).
body.justification: Promise recognition is the genuine unresolved algorithmic boundary left visible by the certifying interface.
body.gap: Neither bounded-size enumeration in Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash nor the solver encodings of Elahi and coauthors classify the complexity of recognizing that no larger minimal hedge exists.
body.consumer: A resolution determines whether low-rank preprocessing can be invoked automatically or must remain a promise-or-counterexample workflow.

obligation.what_is_open: Whether finite simple bow-free singleton ADMG rank-at-most-three recognition is polynomial-time decidable or \(\mathsf{coNP}\)-complete.
obligation.obstruction: The fixed-point oracle decides whether a specified induced vertex set contains a hedge, but neither bounded-size enumeration nor the optimizer's successful feasibility check certifies the global absence of an inclusion-minimal residual of size greater than three. The frozen core contains neither a polynomial absence certificate nor a promise-preserving reduction proving \(\mathsf{coNP}\)-hardness.
obligation.attempted: Alternating ancestor/district restriction and deletion minimization yield explicit large minimal hedges when one is exposed, but they do not force an exposed large hedge on every rank-violating graph without potentially exploring exponentially many deletions. The optimizer-or-violation interface can succeed globally even when another large minimal hedge exists, so success cannot be repurposed as rank recognition.
obligation.partial_result:
There is a polynomial verifier for the complementary language
\(r(G,s)>3\), so deciding \(r(G,s)\leq3\) belongs to \(\mathsf{coNP}\).
Indeed, a certificate is \(F=R\cup\{s\}\) with \(|R|>3\).  Verify by graph
search that \(F\) is a hedge, and for every \(v\in R\) run the fixed-point
hedge oracle on \(F\setminus\{v\}\), accepting only if it returns no hedge.
If a proper hedge \(J\subsetneq F\) existed, some
\(v\in F\setminus J\) would make \(J\subseteq F\setminus\{v\}\), a
contradiction.  Thus the certificate proves
\(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\) and \(|R|>3\).  Conversely, the definition of rank
supplies such a certificate whenever \(r(G,s)>3\).  The certificate has
linear size and requires only polynomially many polynomial-time graph
searches.
